_note: Each line is either traced along the official border (Natural Earth 50m, snapped to the stretches with barrier) or approximate. See geometry_quality per feature. Positions of Belfast interfaces are placeholders placed from street names.

properties.name: Korean Demilitarized Zone
properties.note: Fortified zone established by the 1953 armistice.
properties.construction: Fortified zone: barbed-wire fences, minefields and guard posts; not a continuous wall
properties.initiated_by: 1953 Korean Armistice Agreement (UN Command, North Korea, China)
properties.geometry_quality: official border (whole Natural Earth border; barrier extent not checked)

properties.name: Berlin Wall
properties.note: Encircled West Berlin until November 1989.
properties.construction: Concrete wall (prefabricated concrete slabs) with watchtowers and a cleared 'death strip'

properties.name: Moroccan Western Sahara Wall (Berm)
properties.note: Sand berm built in stages between 1980 and 1987.
properties.construction: Sand berm with fences, minefields and military posts (earthwork, not a wall)

properties.name: India–Bangladesh border fence
properties.note: Construction started in the late 1980s, still being extended.
properties.construction: Mainly barbed-wire fence; some sections with floodlights and patrol roads
properties.geometry_quality: official border (whole Natural Earth border; river sections and fenced extent not checked)

properties.name: Ceuta border fence
properties.note: Raised and reinforced several times since.
properties.construction: Double fence about 6 m high with barbed wire (razor wire partly removed)

properties.name: US–Mexico border barrier
properties.note: Expanded after the 2006 Secure Fence Act and again from 2017.
properties.construction: Steel bollard fence (primary barrier), with secondary barrier in places; older mesh and vehicle barriers replaced
properties.initiated_by: US government (Secure Fence Act 2006 and later programmes)

properties.name: Melilla border fence
properties.note: Triple fence, heightened in 2005.
properties.construction: Double fence 3.5–6 m high with barbed wire; razor wire reintroduced in 2013 on about a third of the perimeter

properties.name: West Bank barrier
properties.note: Mix of concrete wall and fence sections.
properties.construction: About 90% electronic fence (about 2 m) with trenches and patrol road; about 10% concrete wall (8–9 m), mostly in urban areas
properties.geometry_quality: approximate (route inside West Bank not traced)

properties.name: Greece–Turkey Evros fence
properties.note: Initial 12.5 km section, extended from 2020.
properties.construction: Metal fence about 4 m high with razor (blade) wire

properties.name: Saudi–Iraq border barrier
properties.note: Fences, berms and surveillance towers.
properties.construction: Fence with berms and surveillance towers
properties.geometry_quality: official border (whole Natural Earth border; barrier extent not checked)

properties.name: Hungary–Serbia border fence
properties.note: Built during the 2015 migration crisis.
properties.construction: Steel fence about 4 m high, topped with razor wire
properties.geometry_quality: official border (whole Natural Earth border; barrier extent not checked)

properties.name: Turkey–Syria border wall
properties.note: Concrete wall completed around 2018.
properties.construction: Concrete wall with barbed wire, watchtowers and trenches in places
properties.geometry_quality: official border (whole Natural Earth border; barrier extent not checked)

properties.name: Poland–Belarus border barrier
properties.note: Steel barrier completed in 2022.
properties.construction: Steel mesh fence about 5.5 m high with razor wire

properties.name: Finland–Russia border fence
properties.note: Pilot section near Imatra, planned extension to about 200 km.
properties.construction: Steel fence about 3 m high with sensors and cameras

properties.name: Beirut Green Line
properties.note: Divided Beirut between Christian East and Muslim West during the civil war; crossings reopened in 1990.
properties.construction: Barricades of sandbags, rubble and concrete blocks

properties.name: Baghdad Adhamiya wall
properties.note: 3.6 m concrete barrier built by US forces around the Sunni Adhamiya district from April 2007. Iraqi PM al-Maliki asked for it to be halted; it was torn down in 2008. Approximate line.
properties.construction: Concrete blast wall, 3.6 m high
properties.initiated_by: US military (2nd Brigade Combat Team, 82nd Airborne Division)

properties.name: Israel–Gaza perimeter fence
properties.note: Fence and buffer zone along the Gaza border, expanded and upgraded in the 2000s and 2010s. Approximate line.
properties.construction: Fence with concrete barrier sections, sensors and buffer zone; underground barrier added from 2021
